As Brooke settled into the living room sofa to review the blueprint details with Clara, Julian retreated to the quiet corner of the library to organize a stack of historical documents related to the land trust charters. These were the legal foundations of their philanthropic empire, designed to protect community spaces from ever falling back into the hands of real estate speculators.

He picked up a heavy, embossed seal, pressing it down onto a fresh sheet of parchment to test the stamp. The crisp, clean imprint of the foundation's crest—a stylized oak tree with roots anchoring deep into bedrock—stood out sharply against the ivory paper.

Marcus walked in quietly through the open double doors, carrying a sleek metal briefcase that contained nothing more dangerous than quarterly financial reports for the legal aid scholarship fund.

"Looking professional as ever, Julian," Marcus remarked, leaning against the edge of the bookshelf.

"Just dotting the i's and crossing the t's," Julian replied, looking up with a welcoming nod. "How are the scholarship endowments looking for the upcoming academic year?"

"Stronger than projected," Marcus said, taking a seat opposite the desk. "We have enough capital secured to fund full-ride tuition for fifty underprivileged law students at Boston University and Harvard for the next decade. These kids are going to be the next generation of honest reformers."

"Good," Julian murmured, his gaze shifting back to the embossed crest on his desk. "Make sure the selection committee prioritizes applicants who have personal experience with systemic injustice. They're the ones who won't lose their nerve when things get complicated."

Marcus nodded slowly, his expression serious. "Already taken care of. The criteria are ironclad. Nobody's buying their way into this program."
